heading: INT. PARKING GARAGE TICKET BOOTH - NIGHT

units.text: INT. PARKING GARAGE TICKET BOOTH - NIGHT
A glass cubicle at the exit of a nearly empty garage.
Fluorescent hum.
The barrier arm hangs half lowered.
OWEN BRZEZINSKI, fifties, the attendant, sits behind the glass with a crossword.
A hooded WOMAN, thirties, stands at the booth window.
A tall MAN, forties, waits behind her in a long coat, leaning on the pillar.
The woman slides a ticket under the glass.
Owen reads the stamp and frowns.
This ticket is from 1998.
units.name: OWEN

units.text: I know.
units.name: WOMAN

units.text: That's twenty-six years. The fee is, uh, nine thousand dollars.
units.name: OWEN

units.text: I'll pay in cash.
units.name: WOMAN

units.text: She opens her bag.
The man steps closer.
Owen's hand slides toward a button under the counter.
Don't.
units.name: MAN

units.text: Sir, I'm just the attendant.
units.name: OWEN

units.text: He's not talking to you.
units.name: WOMAN

units.text: She pulls out not money but a small silver key and presses it to the glass.
Owen reads the number etched on it.
His face drains.
Where did you get that?
units.name: OWEN

units.text: From the car you parked here that night.
units.name: WOMAN

units.text: The man lunges for the booth door.
Owen hits the button.
An alarm screams.
The woman and the man collide against the glass, shoving, grappling for the key, and both crash into the barrier arm, which snaps.
Police! Parking Garage C!
units.name: OWEN

units.text: The key skids across the concrete.
Owen vaults the counter, scoops it up, and holds it high.
The man and the woman freeze, breathing hard.
Sirens approach, faint, then not so faint.
Give it to me.
units.name: MAN

units.text: No.
units.name: OWEN

units.text: Give it to me, Owen.
units.name: WOMAN

units.text: How do you know my name?
units.name: OWEN

units.text: She pulls back her hood.
A face he hasn't seen in twenty-six years.
Margaret.
units.name: OWEN
